title: Debug graph traversal BFS/DFS bugs — 3 turns
description: BFS and DFS have visited-set bugs causing infinite loops or missing nodes. Fix BFS in turn 1, fix DFS in turn 2, add has_path in turn 3.

files.tests/test_graph.py:
import pytest
from graph import Graph


def test_bfs_simple():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g.add_edge("a", "c")
    g.add_edge("b", "d")
    result = g.bfs("a")
    assert result[0] == "a"
    assert set(result) == {"a", "b", "c", "d"}
    assert len(result) == 4


def test_bfs_no_duplicates():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g.add_edge("b", "c")
    g.add_edge("a", "c")
    result = g.bfs("a")
    assert len(result) == len(set(result))


def test_bfs_isolated_node():
    g = Graph()
    g._adj["x"] = []
    assert g.bfs("x") == ["x"]


def test_dfs_simple():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g.add_edge("a", "c")
    g.add_edge("b", "d")
    result = g.dfs("a")
    assert result[0] == "a"
    assert set(result) == {"a", "b", "c", "d"}
    assert len(result) == 4


def test_dfs_no_duplicates():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g.add_edge("b", "c")
    g.add_edge("a", "c")
    result = g.dfs("a")
    assert len(result) == len(set(result))


def test_has_path_direct():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    assert g.has_path("a", "b") is True


def test_has_path_indirect():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g.add_edge("b", "c")
    assert g.has_path("a", "c") is True


def test_has_path_false():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    g._adj["c"] = []
    assert g.has_path("a", "c") is False


def test_has_path_same_node():
    g = Graph()
    g.add_edge("a", "b")
    assert g.has_path("a", "a") is True

task_spec.prompt: The `bfs()` method in `graph.py` has a visited-set bug: it enqueues neighbors without checking if they're already visited, causing duplicates. Fix `bfs()` so nodes appear exactly once in the result. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_graph.py::test_bfs_simple tests/test_graph.py::test_bfs_no_duplicates -v` to check just the BFS tests.
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` to check the current state. Walk me through what you fixed in BFS. Now fix `dfs()` too — it has no visited set in the recursive helper, which causes infinite loops on cyclic graphs. Fix it, then run the full test suite.

Final step: implement `has_path(src, dst)` — return True if a path exists from src to dst (use BFS or DFS). Also handle the case where src == dst. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` — all 9 tests must pass.
success_criteria: BFS returns each node exactly once (no duplicates)
DFS returns each node exactly once (visited set prevents infinite loop)
has_path returns True for connected nodes
has_path returns False for disconnected nodes
